findings: Conditional refill-deficit proof closes the previously conservative national-to-district bridge inside the original fixed-eight-party transfer domain.
National minima 9,086 (2022) and 10,269 (2026) also bound the full 29-district engine in that domain; unrestricted election-law optimization is not established.
A dated family can already permit both directed targets at cost zero, while imposing one common target in every world requires a positive-cost witness or can be structurally impossible.
Both statement-only January 2019 families contain the all-party nonrejecting world with 349 nonrejecting seats; therefore common rejection is impossible while that role family remains fixed.

limitations: Only the original fixed-eight-party, district-turnout/quotas and role domain is certified. Candidate-list capacities, new-party entry/exit and turnout changes are excluded.
The native replay reuses the existing election core and rejects relevant ties; the proof bounds all legal tie completions without enumerating all intermediate tie paths.
2019 multi-world positive costs are bounds, not exact minima. Source-only and research-assumption families remain distinct.
Cost zero for an any-world directed target is not an identified outcome-flip margin when the baseline family is already ambiguous.
